validity.recommendation: Change Length to 637 km (the gas main) and CapacityUnits to bcm/y; remove the SKhV page as a Length reference only after a person checks it
validity.researcher_notes: The 472 km Length is the Komsomolsk-on-Amur to Khabarovsk branch of the Sakhalin-Khabarovsk-Vladivostok system, per the Energy Policy article the sheet already cites. The Trans-Sakhalin gas main is 637 km, 1220 mm, 18.6 bcm/y in the same article. The sheet's Length reference (Gazprom's page on the Sakhalin-Khabarovsk-Vladivostok system) is therefore about the wrong pipeline. The Capacity unit mtpa is wrong for a gas pipeline. The pipeline is real and operating. The row is a system row, and the wiki's 856 km counts all gathering and transmission segments.

fills.researcher_notes: The Energy Policy article of June 2024 (read through the July 2025 Wayback capture, the live page now redirects to the site home) says the Trans-Sakhalin gas main is 637 km long, 1220 mm in diameter, with a design capacity of 18.6 billion cubic meters a year. The sheet holds 18.60 with the unit mtpa, which is a tonnes unit and does not fit a gas pipeline. The figure matches the article exactly in bcm/y, so the unit is restored to bcm/y. The article is a single source and it is the same one already on the sheet.

fills.researcher_notes: The Energy Policy article says the Trans-Sakhalin gas main route is 637 km. The sheet holds 472 km. The 472 km figure in that same article belongs to a different pipeline, the Komsomolsk-on-Amur to Khabarovsk branch of the Sakhalin-Khabarovsk-Vladivostok system, and the sheet's current reference for Length (the Gazprom page on that system) is about the wrong pipeline. The wiki page lists 637 km for its Segment II and 856 km for all segments together. The operator page gives only combined oil and gas totals (283 km offshore and 1,591 km onshore), which is not a figure for the gas line. The value is changed to 637 km on the one article. The old value and the reason are in the validity note.

fills.researcher_notes: The operator's overview page says Sakhalin Energy Limited Liability Company is the operator of the Sakhalin-2 project and that oil and gas move through the Trans-Sakhalin pipeline system. A Polish Centre for Eastern Studies analysis of April 2023 says the Russian company Sakhalinskaya Energiya became the project operator on 30 June 2022 under a presidential decree. Neither page is a table about the pipeline alone, so the tier is medium.

fills.researcher_notes: The operator's overview page names Sakhalin Energy LLC as the company running the Sakhalin-2 project and its Trans-Sakhalin pipeline system. It does not use the word owner, so the tier is medium. The Reuters articles of April 2023 and March 2024 only describe the sale of Shell's former 27.5 percent share in the project company, which is a shareholder change above the owner recorded here and does not change it.
